correctness.rationale: The invariant I1 equations from the primary Potts boundary-law construction are h=k f_theta(h), l=f_theta(h)+(k-1)f_theta(l), with f_theta(x)=log((theta exp x+2)/(theta+exp x+1)). Both t=exp(h/k)>0 and y=exp(l/(k-1))/t^(1/(k-1))>0 are bijective coordinate transformations. The first polynomial F=t^(k+1)-theta t^k+(theta+1)t-2 has ≤3 positive roots by Descartes, and the strict signs at 0,2/theta,1,theta/2,theta for k≥4 theta>24 locate roots t_-<1<t_+. For every such t, H_t(y)=t y^k-theta t y^(k-1)+(theta+1)y-2 has ≤3 positive roots; strict sign brackets (0,1,theta/2,∞) when t<1, (0,1/2,2,∞) at t=1, and (0,3/theta,1,∞) when t>1 supply 3 each. The uniform bound theta>24 makes all inequalities strict (including H_(t+)(3/theta)>1-24/theta>0), proving exactly nine distinct pairs for every k≥4. Independently checked rational F endpoint signs for all 4≤k≤8 and theta=25,30,50; these finite signs are corroboration, not the infinite proof.
